title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.33). Grothendieck is building a combinatorial axiomatics for 'Analysis situs'. The data are a set M of 'multiplicités' with two relations. The first is ≪, an order relation, read as incidence or 'lies in the closure of'. The second is R_M, a symmetric reflexive relation called 'compatibility'. One sets X ≤ Y iff X ≪ Y and X is compatible with Y. Cont 1 requires ≤ to be an order. A family 𝓕 of subsets of M, the 'figures', is then axiomatised:
- Cont 2: a figure is pairwise compatible and is a 'partie finissante' (downward-closed subset) of (M, ≤).
- Cont 3: a downward-closed subset of a figure is a figure (sub-figure); the empty set is a figure.
- Fig 1: for each X, the set M_{≤X} is a figure, the 'elementary figure' of X.
On p.33 he derives that two elements below a common X and compatible with X are mutually compatible.

This page.
- (Fig 4 / Cont 4) If F and G are figures such that every X∈F is compatible with every Y∈G ('compatible figures'), then F∪G is a figure. F∩G is automatically a common sub-figure: it is downward closed and contained in F, so Cont 3 applies.
- A crossed-out corollary states hereditary compatibility: if X'≪X, Y'≪Y, X and Y are compatible, and X',X and Y',Y are compatible, then X' and Y' are compatible.
- 'Contraintes finitistes': all figures are finite.
- Corollary: under the finitist constraint, the figures are exactly the finite, pairwise compatible, downward-closed (for ≤) subsets of M. One direction is Cont 2. Conversely, a finite downward-closed pairwise compatible S is the union of the finitely many elementary figures M_{≤X}, X∈S. These are pairwise compatible figures, so by iterated Fig 4 (and 'empty is a figure') S is a figure. This converse direction does not even need finitism, only finiteness of S.
- Hence, under finitism, the whole structure 𝓕 is determined by (≪, R_M) alone.
- He then reverses the question. Start from an order ≪ and a symmetric reflexive relation R_M satisfying Cont 1, and define the 'configurations' as the finite downward-closed pairwise compatible subsets. Under what conditions on (≪, R_M) do the configurations satisfy Cont 2–Cont 5? Cont 2, 3 and 4 hold trivially for configurations. The real content is Fig 1: M_{≤X} must be finite, and its elements mutually compatible (the hereditary-compatibility property). This is exactly what p.35 imposes: Cond 3', 'M_{≤X} is finite', with a finite combinatorial dimension condition, followed by 'lieux' (≪-minimal elements, i.e. points) and 'ombres' (shadows) in Cond 4.

Purpose: a purely combinatorial model of a stratified or tame space. Elements play the role of strata or cells, ≪ the closure/incidence relation, and figures the finite subcomplexes. Lieux are points, and the ombre of X is its set of points.
errors: The corollary must read 'downward closed for ≤' (or saturated for ≤), not for ≪. A subset downward closed for ≪ in M would contain incompatible elements and could not be pairwise compatible. The transcription's 'mutuellement décroissantes pour ≪' is either a misreading or a slip.

Minor: the converse half of the corollary (finite configurations are figures) uses only Fig 1, Fig 4 and the empty figure, not finitism. Finitism is needed only for 'every figure is a configuration'. The text is not wrong, just not sharp on this point.
The labels 'Cond'/'Cont' are used inconsistently across the transcription. The axioms are 'Cont' (contraintes), while the next page switches to 'Cond.'.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'figures' in a set with an order ≪ and a symmetric reflexive compatibility relation; figures are pairwise compatible downward-closed subsets, stable under sub-figures and unions of compatible figures
ideas.modern_name: Abstract (partial) cell or simplicial complexes via face posets; closest exact match: configurations of a prime event structure (causality ≤, conflict = non-compatibility), or cliques of a coherence space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Event structures: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981), Winskel (1980s). Coherence spaces: Girard (1986–87). Face posets of regular CW complexes: classical (Björner and others)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1986 Analysis situs notes; unsure whether anything similar appears in other circulated texts

ideas.what: Under finitism, figures are exactly the finite downward-closed pairwise compatible subsets ('configurations'), so the structure is determined by (≪, R_M)
ideas.modern_name: Finite configurations of an event structure / finite cliques generated by principal ideals

ideas.what: Inverse problem: conditions on (≪, R_M) making configurations satisfy the figure axioms; the answer on p.35 is finiteness of principal ideals M_{≤X} plus hereditary compatibility
ideas.modern_name: Finite-causes axiom and conflict inheritance for prime event structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axioms for multiplicités and figures are essentially the axioms of prime event structures. The match covers causality ≤ (with ≪ as an extra coarser order), compatibility as the complement of conflict, configurations as finite downward-closed conflict-free sets (he even uses the word 'configurations'), the finiteness of M_{≤X} on the next page (Winskel's finite-causes axiom), and hereditary compatibility (conflict inheritance). The lieux/ombre structure on p.35 adds a geometric 'support on points' layer absent from event structures. To my knowledge no one has related Grothendieck's late Analysis situs axiomatics to event structures or coherence spaces, which have since acquired geometric and homotopical interpretations (e.g. higher-dimensional automata, directed topology).
missed.quote: les parties finies saturées et formées d'éléments mut. compatibles (ici les configurations) satisfont-elles Cond 2 à Cond 5 ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a bridge between Grothendieck's combinatorial approach to tame or stratified spaces and concurrency theory and directed algebraic topology, where configuration posets of event structures are studied geometrically. It is a curiosity rather than a new theorem.

missed.claim: The page poses the realisation question: characterise those pairs (≪, R_M) whose configurations form a figure system satisfying all the contraintes. It is answered only partially on p.35 (Cond 3', Cond 3, Cond 4). The full theory of such 'multiplicités' as models of tame spaces is not developed in the literature.
missed.quote: à quelles conditions les parties finies saturées et formées d'éléments mut. compatibles ... satisfont-elles Cond 2 à Cond 5 ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early version of Grothendieck's combinatorial foundations for 'topologie modérée'. This is of historical interest; mathematically it is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary poset and complex bookkeeping, and the corollary is routine. The mildly notable point is the near-exact coincidence with prime event structures and their configurations, developed independently in computer science at the same time. That link has apparently not been remarked upon.
transcription_corrections: '(cf Cond 2, Cond 3, Cond 5)' should read '(cf Cont 2, Cont 3, Cont 5)'. Likewise 'Cond 1' and 'Cond 2 à Cond 5' at the bottom are 'Cont 1' and 'Cont 2 à Cont 5' in the image.
The crossed label before 'Soient F et G' is probably 'Cont 4' (crossed), with '(Fig 4)' circled above it, not 'Cond 2'.
Left margin, written diagonally: 'On dit alors que F et G sont des figures compatibles' (correctly captured).
The corollary line likely reads 'les parties finies de M, formées [d'éléments] ... décroissantes [saturées] pour ≤, et mutuellement compatibles'. Mathematically it must be ≤, not ≪.
'Donc, sous contraintes finitistes, [la structure] est connue par les seules structures ≪, R_M (ordre, et rel. sym. réfl.)': the parenthetical describes ≪ as an order and R_M as symmetric reflexive.
The page header line 'Contraintes finitistes ... telles que toute figure' is entirely crossed out.
